scope: Selected explanations for temporal context, not a ranking of causal probability. Treatment dates come from the prepared public timeline; biological sources do not establish a cause of Sid’s measured changes.

treatments.title: Metformin
treatments.explanation: Metformin lowers blood sugar, and human research has linked its use to differences in gut bacteria. It could be relevant to the observed community change.

candidateNotes.bifido: That study reported higher B. bifidum in metformin users. This makes the species breakdown worth examining, but does not establish that metformin caused Sid’s change.
candidateNotes.akk: The study’s Akkermansia finding concerns A. muciniphila; equivalence to Sid’s KLE1798 annotation is unconfirmed.

treatments.title: Cefazolin
treatments.explanation: Cefazolin is an antibiotic. Its prescribing information notes that antibacterial treatment can alter the colon’s bacterial community, so it is a possible contributor to investigate. This does not predict which bacterial groups would increase or decrease.

treatments.title: Dalbavancin
treatments.explanation: Dalbavancin treats bacterial infections. However, a small single-dose study in healthy volunteers found no major overall effect on intestinal flora. Its timing is useful context, but it is a weak explanation for a large shift.

treatments.title: Wegovy
treatments.explanation: Wegovy affects appetite and slows stomach emptying. Changes in food intake or digestion could be relevant context, but this does not establish a direct effect on any of these bacterial groups.

treatments.title: Zepbound
treatments.explanation: Zepbound affects appetite and slows stomach emptying. Food intake and digestion are possible indirect links to explore; no specific bacterial effect is established here.
